commands.name: add

options.name: --path
options.description: Specify the path where the file will be created. If  not specified, it will be created in the current directory.

commands.name: config

options.name: --name
options.description: The name of the journal. If not specified, uses  the directory name.

options.name: --toc
options.description: The name of the table of contents file to parse  (without .md extension). If not specified, uses the default name.

commands.description: Creates a new journal configuration file if one does  not already exist

commands.name: entry

options.name: --he
options.description: The heading that the new entry will fall under in  the table of contents. If the subheading option is also specified then the  heading will prepend to that.

options.name: --ignore
options.description: This flag makes it so the new entry won't  appear in the table of contents.

options.name: --sh
options.description: The subheadings that the new entry will fall under in the table of contents. Nested subheadings must be seperated by - and if a  subheading has multiple words the spaces must be seperated by _. ex:  heading_one-heading_two. If the heading option is also specified the subheading  will append to that.

options.name: --title
options.description: The title of the journal entry. use this if  it's different than the file name.

arguments.name: name
arguments.description: The name of the journal entry to create. This will be used in both the file name and the entry TOC title unless title option is  specified.

examples: add --path Source/Repos/TestJournal entry Meeting_Notes --heading  Work --subheading Team-Standup

commands.name: remove

options.name: --path
options.description: Specify the path of the journal. If not specified, it  will default to the current directory.

commands.name: entry

options.name: --clean-refs
options.description: Scan all other entry files and strip inline links  pointing to the removed entry.

options.name: --force
options.description: Skip the confirmation prompt and remove  immediately.

arguments.name: fileName

Removes a specified file from an existing journal.

commands.name: update

options.name: --path
options.description: Specify the path of the journal. If not specified, it  will default to the current directory.

commands.name: entry

options.name: --he
options.description: The new location in the TOC hierarchy. Use - to  separate heading levels and _ for spaces within heading names. Example:  'Projects-2024_Goals' creates nested headings. If you use spaces  without - separators, the entire string is treated as a single heading.  Recommended: use _ for clarity.

options.name: --ignore
options.description: Add this entry to the ignore list so it won't appear in the table of contents.

options.name: --name
options.description: The new name for the entry (last filename segment  only). Updates both the file name and TOC title when they currently match,  unless --title is also specified. To change the heading location use  -h|--headings.

options.name: --nb
options.description: Skip updating inline link references in other  entry files after a rename. Backlink updates are enabled by default.

options.name: --title
options.description: The title of the journal entry. This is the name  that will show on the TOC.

options.name: --unignore
options.description: Remove this entry from the ignore list so it will  appear in the table of contents.

arguments.name: fileName
arguments.description: The name of the file you want to update. this can  be with or without the .md file extension.

examples: update --path Source/Repos/TestJournal entry OldFileName --name  NewFileName --headings Projects-Completed_Tasks

commands.name: journal

options.name: --config
options.description: Flag to update the config.

options.name: --date
options.description: Flag to update the markdown "Last  Edited:" metadata and related tracking for modified files.

options.name: --dry-run
options.description: Preview what would change without applying any  updates. Shows added, modified, and removed files for each requested section.  Respects all other flags for scoping (e.g. --dry-run --config shows only config  drift). --check is an alias.

options.name: --rename-toc
options.description: Rename the table-of-contents file to  <name> (stem only, no extension). Updates .journalrc, rewrites all  markdown inline link references, and stamps Last Edited on modified files.

options.name: --sync
options.description: Update tracking index, config, and table of  contents without writing "Last Edited:" to user entry files. Designed  for post-git-pull / post-merge scenarios where file hashes may be stale but  entries have not been genuinely edited.

options.name: --toc
options.description: Flag to update the table of contents.

options.name: --tracking
options.description: Updates file tracking independently without  touching "Last Edited:" metadata. This overrides --date if both are  specified, leaving file metadata unchanged.

commands.description: Updates configuration, table of contents, and Last  Edited dates metadata. All items are updated by default unless specific flags  are provided
Updates various aspects of an existing journal.
